title: Silent Payments: one address, no reuse
host: Razor and keypleb, with guest Sosthène (Dana wallet)
summary: A live silent payment from Cake Wallet to Shroud, a guest who builds the Dana wallet on what silent payments fix (and what they don't), and Razor rebuilding the protocol from scratch: tweaked keys, Diffie-Hellman, Taproot. Plus where you can help.
share_text: Silent Payments: one static Bitcoin address, a fresh Taproot output every time, nothing to link. Live demo, a from-scratch build of the protocol, and 4 mini-games. Notes from the @CodeOrangeDevs Privacy Track
tldr: A silent payment address starts with sp1 and can be posted anywhere. Every payment to it lands on a different, normal-looking Taproot output, so nobody can list your payments.
It fixes address reuse, the baseline privacy leak. It does not stop chain analysis if you later merge those coins, so pair it with coin control, PayJoin and other tools.

Sending is easy and needs no node. Receiving is the hard part: your wallet has to scan every transaction, and how it scans (full node, Electrum server, BlindBit) decides what you leak and how fast you see payments.
The projects are run by very few people: Dana, BlindBit Oracle, Frigate and Shroud all welcome new contributors.
chapters: Welcome and the plan for today
Live demo: Cake Wallet to Shroud, then mempool.space
Why some wallets see a payment sooner: scanning
Address reuse, and what silent payments don't fix
Spot the silent payment: Taproot outputs and round amounts
Gap limits, with a real wallet recovery story
Razor's deep dive: history and the interactivity scale
Sender vs receiver: why scanning is the hard part
How to contribute: Dana, BlindBit, Frigate, Shroud

todo.title: Try it before next time
items: Get a silent payment address (it starts with sp1) in Cake Wallet, Sparrow, Dana or Shroud.
Send a few thousand sats to it, then look the transaction up on mempool.space. Can you tell it apart from a normal Taproot payment?
Read the overview on silentpayments.xyz. Brave? Open BIP 352.
Pick one project (Dana, BlindBit Oracle, Frigate or the Shroud indexer), build it and run it. That is how contributing starts.

resources.title: Sparrow Wallet

resources.title: BlindBit Oracle
resources.note: a silent payments indexing server that only serves public data, so it learns very little about you. Can't see mempool payments yet

resources.title: Frigate
resources.note: Electrum server for silent payments, the backend behind Sparrow. Scans for you, so you trade some privacy for speed

ideas: Also on the call: why you might skip the Bitcoin t-shirt at the airport, why France has seen home invasions targeting crypto holders this year, and a tip for asking to be paid: add a few random sats so the amount is not round. Guest speaker Anmol (Shroud wallet) could not make it this time.

quiz.q: In silent payments, does the sender have to notify the receiver before paying?
o: No, the receiver finds the payment by scanning
quiz.w: That is the whole point: almost no interaction. BIP 47 needed a notification transaction; silent payments don't.

quiz.q: Which leak do silent payments protect you from?
quiz.w: Silent payments stop address reuse. Breaking the common input heuristic is what PayJoin does.

quiz.q: What output type does a silent payment create?
quiz.w: Taproot. Razor's slides used P2PK to explain the idea, but real silent payments always land on a Taproot output.

o: Senders must run a full node
The receiver has to do much more work to scan for payments
Addresses can only be used once
quiz.w: Senders need no node. Receivers must check every transaction, which is why scanning backends matter so much.

quiz.q: Your friend pays 20,000 sats and gets 3,026 sats change. What gives the payment away?
quiz.w: Round numbers (in sats or in fiat at that moment) look human-entered. Ask for a few extra random sats to blur it.
